questions.question: Why prefer type="email" over type="text" for an email field?

options.text: It gives native validation (@ check), email keyboard on mobile, and autofill hints
It prevents all invalid input permanently

questions.explanation: Semantic input types trigger browser validation, optimized mobile keyboards, and password-manager/autofill detection.

questions.question: Which attribute restricts a number input to values between 1 and 10?
questions.explanation: min/max set the allowed bounds for number/range/date inputs. step controls increment granularity.

questions.question: What does input type="range" render and what attributes control it?

options.text: A text box; controlled by size
A slider; min, max, step, value

questions.explanation: type="range" shows a slider bounded by min/max with step increments; value sets the initial position.

questions.question: A file input with accept=".pdf,.docx" multiple allows users to:

options.text: Select multiple files filtered to PDF/DOCX types

questions.explanation: accept hints the file picker filter; multiple enables selecting several files. The actual upload needs a form/JS.

questions.question: If a browser doesn't support type="date", what happens?

options.text: It falls back to a plain text input

questions.explanation: Unknown input types degrade gracefully to type="text", so you should still validate server-side and/or with JS.

questions.question: Which input type triggers a numeric keypad with symbols (good for phone numbers)?
questions.explanation: type="tel" shows a telephone-optimized numeric keypad. type="number" can also show digits but tel is semantically for phone.

questions.question: What is the <input type="color"> element used for?

options.text: Opening a native color picker returning a hex value like #ff0000

questions.explanation: type="color" opens a color picker and the value is a hex string (e.g. #ff0000).

questions.question: Even with built-in validation, why must you STILL validate on the server?

options.text: Because client-side validation can be bypassed (disabled JS, crafted requests)

questions.explanation: Client validation is a UX convenience and is trivially bypassed; authoritative validation must happen server-side.
